source.title: Understanding Short-Range Memory Effects in Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: C. Tan; Jiang-She Zhang; Jun-Min Liu

record.tranche_reason: The study varies batch size and learning rate and measures Hurst parameter, Hessian curvature, and test accuracy, bearing conceptually on batch-size effects and measured properties associated with generalization.
record.gate_note: The paper does not test memorization of random labels, widening past interpolation, architecture comparisons for test error, optimizer comparisons, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. Its own test-accuracy results are shown in figures; the prose descriptions of large-batch generalization are cited background, not this study’s results.
record.test_reason: The study measures gradient-noise memory, Hessian eigenvalues, and test accuracy, but does not test any listed version under its defining conditions. In particular, training stops when cross-entropy loss reaches 0.01 rather than after a fixed epoch budget, so its batch-size comparisons do not test V5. Hessian curvature and Hurst estimates do not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness or generalization-gap ranking.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate as a paraphrase of the authors' position. They propose modeling SGD with fractional Brownian motion, report evidence of gradient-noise memory across architectures and training strategies, and associate larger Hurst estimates with smaller Hessian eigenvalues. Their approximate first-passage analysis suggests longer residence in wide minima. They leave further analysis of generalization properties to future work.
record.recipe_differences: Measures stochastic-gradient-noise memory and related Hurst parameter, curvature, and test accuracy; it does not reproduce the claim’s random-label or fixed-epoch generalization experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The estimated Hurst parameter varies with batch size, learning rate, model capacity, and training strategy. Test-accuracy plots vary batch size and learning rate.

fits_no_version.finding: Figures 12–13 compare test accuracy across batch sizes for ResNet18 and VGG16_BN on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100. The default stopping rule is cross-entropy loss below 0.01; curve values and directions cannot be reliably reconstructed from the supplied text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch size affects held-out accuracy when networks are trained to a common training-loss threshold.

fits_no_version.finding: Section IV-C and Figure 9 report increasing largest Hessian eigenvalues and decreasing Hurst estimates with batch size for an FCN on MNIST and AlexNet on CIFAR-10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Estimated gradient-noise memory covaries inversely with unscaled Hessian curvature across batch-size settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Width and depth change FCN Hurst estimates; CNN scale, learning rate, momentum, and weight decay are also examined for their effects on Hurst estimates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient-noise memory estimates depend on architecture and training hyperparameters.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems
record.problems: Test-accuracy and Hurst trends are presented in plots without numerical values in the text. Experiments are run three times and plotted as means; uncertainty is not described for the model experiments.
record.rows_left_out: No result rows retained: the study’s own test-accuracy outcomes are only plotted, and the supplied text does not give recoverable values or explicit outcome descriptions for the batch-size and learning-rate comparisons. The cited large-batch generalization findings are prior work. Test-accuracy plots appear in Figs. 11–15.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error; width experiments report Hurst estimates instead.
Controlled convolutional versus fully connected test-error comparisons and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning conditions.
Large-batch held-out performance under a fixed epoch budget and recovery through recipe adaptations. The study uses a training-loss stopping threshold.
Dropout effects on held-out error, including small-data and augmentation regimes.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, its association with training-to-test gaps, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized versus random training examples.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied figure text contains axes and captions but does not preserve readable curves. These plots are already declared in rows_left_out, so they are not added as missing results. Statements that large batches generalize poorly are background claims, not explicit descriptions of this study's accuracy outcomes.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width beyond the interpolation threshold and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected test error and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and tuning or weight-decay effects.
The paper varies batch size and plots test accuracy, but does not report fixed-epoch comparisons or recoverable test-accuracy values in the supplied text.
Dropout and weight-decay effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbation sharpness and comparison with norm- or margin-based measures.
Removing examples most memorized by the network and measuring test accuracy.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
